shots.title: Run roadmap validation, targeted issue regressions, and full release-readiness checks
shots.notes: Release-readiness baseline passed: roadmap validation, targeted S216-S221 regressions, typecheck, full Vitest, build, map check, version recommendation, and pre-bump package dry-run signal.

shots.title: Bump package and bundled plugin manifest according to version recommendation
shots.notes: Root package and bundled Codex plugin manifest were bumped to 1.60.0, the built CLI reported v1.60.0, and npm dry-run passed for the unpublished version.

shots.title: Publish the recovery release and update roadmap next-lane status

hazards.description: The release branch was five commits behind main and reused an old merged PR branch name, so publication required a fresh release worktree, a new branch, and a roadmap merge that preserved S153/S154 while adding S216-S222.
pnpm 11 generated a local allowBuilds workspace file during npm dry-run; the dry-run passed after local approval and the generated file was removed from the release diff.

shots.notes: The release branch codex/recovery-release-v1.60.0 is pushed with mainline S153/S154 integrated, S155-S158 marked superseded by the executed S216-S222 train, and v1.60.0 package dry-run verified.

conditions.description: The release branch had to reconcile the executed S216-S222 recovery train with mainline S153/S154 and the already-published v1.59.2 baseline.

training.description: Release branches should be rebased or merged from main before the final version bump.
training.outcome: S222 used a fresh release worktree and branch to isolate the merge from unrelated dirty files in the original checkout.

training.description: Roadmap recovery lanes can collide when main advances during a long issue train.
training.outcome: The merged roadmap keeps S154 as shipped, marks S155-S158 superseded, and makes S216-S222 the executed Phase 49 recovery train.

training.description: pnpm 11 build approval state can affect npm dry-run in fresh worktrees.
training.outcome: The release dry-run used local allowBuilds approval for native build scripts and removed the generated workspace file from version control.

nutrition.description: Pre-merge targeted S216-S221 regressions passed: 26 files, 340 tests.
Merged release branch focused suite passed: 10 files, 216 tests.
Merged release branch full Vitest passed: 238 files, 3746 tests, with store-pg skipped by configuration.
Merged release branch passed typecheck, build, roadmap validate, map --check, version smoke, and npm publish --dry-run --access public for @slope-dev/slope@1.60.0.

nineteenth_hole.how_did_it_feel: The release gate did its job: the feature train was ready, but mainline drift had to be made explicit before publishing.
nineteenth_hole.advice_for_next_player: Cut the release branch from current main, then replay or merge the recovery train before the final dry-run.
nineteenth_hole.what_surprised_you: The roadmap conflict was mostly planning metadata, not implementation code; a structured JSON merge was safer than hand-splicing markers.
nineteenth_hole.excited_about_next: After the PR merges, the GitHub Release workflow can publish v1.60.0 through trusted publishing and verify npm latest.

bunker_locations: Do not reuse an old merged PR branch name for a release train; create a fresh release branch before PR publication.
When main already has a planned issue lane, merge the executed lane by marking stale planned sprints superseded instead of deleting their planning context.
Fresh pnpm 11 worktrees may need local allowBuilds approval before npm publish dry-run can run lifecycle builds.
yardage_book_updates: docs/backlog/roadmap.json now merges mainline S154 with the executed S216-S222 train and marks S155-S158 superseded.
tests/cli/sprint-workflow.test.ts now aligns the all-gates-complete status regression with review-gate provenance requirements.
The release branch codex/recovery-release-v1.60.0 is pushed for PR publication.
course_management_notes: S222 release-readiness evidence includes targeted regressions, full suite, typecheck, build, roadmap validation, map check, version smoke, npm registry latest check, and npm dry-run.
npm latest reported 1.59.2 before release; v1.60.0 is the next publish target.
No direct local npm publish was run; publication should happen through the GitHub Release to npm trusted-publishing workflow after merge.
